p-tau217/PET discordance has direction-specific meaning

Across 1,069 cognitively normal adults, plasma p-tau217-positive/PET-negative and p-tau217-negative/PET-positive profiles carried different biomarker and longitudinal signals, and the p-tau217 operating point changed their interpretation.

Key quantitative results: The combined analysis included 1,069 cognitively normal adults: 594 in CPAS and 475 in ADNI.

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217Aβ42/40Discordance interpretation

Added October 22, 2026 · DOI:10.1002/alz.71922; PMID:42902436

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Discordance was not a single intermediate state. p-tau217-positive/PET-negative participants had higher GFAP and NfL, whereas p-tau217-negative/PET-positive participants showed lower plasma Aβ42/40 in ADNI. Both p-tau217-positive groups had greater clinical-progression risk, while both PET-positive groups accumulated amyloid faster. The p-tau217-positive/PET-negative accumulation signal appeared only with less-specific cutoffs, underscoring that assay operating points shape discordance.

Study design

Investigators analyzed 594 cognitively normal adults from CPAS and 475 from ADNI. Amyloid PET positivity was defined as at least 20 Centiloids; cohort-specific p-tau217 cutoffs were anchored to PET at at least 90% specificity. Cross-sectional plasma, imaging and cognitive profiles were compared across four concordance groups, with mixed-effects and Cox models applied to longitudinal ADNI imaging, cognition and clinical progression.

Key quantitative results

  • The combined analysis included 1,069 cognitively normal adults: 594 in CPAS and 475 in ADNI.
  • Relative to p-tau217-negative/PET-negative participants, the p-tau217-positive/PET-negative group had higher GFAP and NfL in both cohorts, while the p-tau217-negative/PET-positive group had lower plasma Aβ42/40 in ADNI.
  • In ADNI, both p-tau217-positive groups had higher clinical-progression risk and faster decline in selected cognitive domains; both PET-positive groups showed faster Centiloid accumulation.
  • Faster Centiloid accumulation in the p-tau217-positive/PET-negative group was observed only when lower-specificity p-tau217 thresholds were used.

What changed

The publication separates the two directions of p-tau217/PET discordance and demonstrates that their biological and prognostic meaning depends partly on the chosen p-tau217 operating point.

Strength of evidence

Moderate clinical-validity evidence from two sizable cohorts, strengthened by longitudinal ADNI follow-up. Clinical utility remains unproven because thresholds were cohort-specific, outcome effects were observational, and no discordance-guided clinical decision strategy was tested.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

A discordant result should be interpreted by direction, assay and cutoff rather than labeled generically as uncertain. Consequential results still require clinical correlation and confirmatory amyloid testing when definitive pathology status is needed.

Field medical relevance

Directly addresses blood–PET concordance, cutoff selection, sequential testing and the distinction between risk enrichment and confirmed amyloid pathology.

Quanterix or platform relevance

p-tau217 positivity used cohort-specific PET-anchored cutoffs selected for at least 90% specificity. The study therefore evaluates operating-point-dependent discordance rather than establishing a transferable assay cutoff.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No authorization, availability, reimbursement or coverage change. The findings refine interpretation rather than creating an ordering pathway.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does p-tau217-positive/PET-negative mean early amyloid accumulation?
Not reliably. Faster Centiloid accumulation in that group appeared only at lower-specificity p-tau217 thresholds, so the interpretation depends on the assay operating point and may also reflect non-amyloid injury signals.
Does a discordant blood result replace amyloid PET?
No. The study supports direction-specific risk interpretation but explicitly requires validation before clinical use and does not establish a replacement rule.
Can these cutoffs be transferred to another assay?
No. Positivity was defined with cohort-specific PET-anchored cutoffs, not universal concentrations.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Cognitively normal cohorts limit generalizability to symptomatic specialty care
  • Cohort-specific p-tau217 assays and cutoffs
  • Longitudinal analyses were available in ADNI rather than both cohorts
  • The abstract does not provide absolute event rates or model effect estimates
  • No prospective test of discordance-guided clinical management
